episode_title: Major Update: No More Minor Issue After Landmark Ruling!

real_qa.q: What did Italy's Supreme Court United Sections rule regarding minor age and Italian citizenship loss in 2024?
real_qa.r: The United Sections of Italy's Supreme Court established that the minor age of a child whose ancestor becomes naturalized no longer causes loss of Italian citizenship. The court determined that the age of the child when the parent becomes naturalized is irrelevant, meaning the child can retain Italian citizenship together with citizenship they were born with if born abroad, regardless of whether they were underage when the parent naturalized.
real_qa.requete: Italy Supreme Court minor age citizenship ruling

real_qa.q: When did Italy change the legal age of majority from 21 to 18 years old?
real_qa.r: The age of majority in Italy was 21 years of age until 1975, when the law changed and the age of majority became 18 years old. Anyone under 21 was considered a minor before 1975.
real_qa.requete: Italy age of majority 1975 changed from 21 to 18

real_qa.q: How does the Supreme Court minor age ruling affect Italian citizenship cases pending at consulates?
real_qa.r: Those with cases pending at Italian consulates affected by the minor age issue can now realistically expect their cases to be approved. The Italian Ministry of Interior will likely issue new guidelines (circolare) soon to instruct consulates to follow the Supreme Court's decision, as consulates previously followed precise instructions from the Ministry to reject these cases.
real_qa.requete: Supreme Court minor age ruling Italian consulate citizenship approval

real_qa.q: Can the Supreme Court minor age ruling be used to appeal rejected Italian citizenship cases?
real_qa.r: Yes, anyone who recently received a rejection from an Italian consulate or civil court because of the minor age issue can now appeal with confidence, as their case will be approved based on the recent Supreme Court ruling. If a judge already wrote the text of a ruling denying the case, applicants can appeal based on the most recent Supreme Court decision.
real_qa.requete: appeal rejected Italian citizenship minor age Supreme Court ruling

real_qa.q: How does the Supreme Court minor age ruling interact with Italy's Tajani Decree?
real_qa.r: The Supreme Court ruling was rendered regarding the old rules under the previous framework. However, cases presented under the new Tajani Decree framework can no longer be denied based on the minor age issue. The Tajani Decree is currently being challenged in the Italian Constitutional Court and European Court of Justice, so the full impact on new rules remains unclear pending further clarifications.
real_qa.requete: Tajani Decree minor age Supreme Court ruling interaction
